<!-- pr-coding-standards-review -->

**Coding-standards review**

Reviewed `smartcontractkit/chainlink#23832` against `.github/copilot-instructions.md` at `develop`.

3 inline finding(s).

comments.body:
**High** - Correctness

`pruneStaleShims` unconditionally calls `w.registry.Remove(ctx, key.capID)` keyed only by capability ID, but the registry entry for that ID may not be the pruned combined client: `registry.Add` errors on a duplicate ID (per the PR's own comment), so when a capID is hosted by two remote capability DONs (the state `warnOnDuplicateInFamilyCapabilities` anticipates) or collides with a locally registered capability, the cached client for the stale DON is pruned while the surviving client's registration is nil'd out and never re-added (`getCombinedClient` returns `isNewCC=false`, so `registry.Add` is skipped)

**Standard:** "Does the code do what the PR claims, for every input and state it can receive, including edge, empty, and failure cases? Do invariants still hold after every path?"

**Fix:** before removing, confirm the registry entry actually belongs to the pruned client (e.g. `registry.Get` and compare identity) and, when another cached CombinedClient for the same capID survives, re-register that client (or track which single shimID owns the registry entry, e.g. the lowest DON ID) instead of blindly calling `registry.Remove`.

<!-- pr-coding-standards-review -->

**High** - Correctness

when a per-method shim is pruned while its capability/DON stays, the shim is closed and deregistered from the dispatcher but left wired into its CombinedClient (`combinedClient.triggerSubscribers`/`executableClients` still map the method to the closed shim), so `RegisterTrigger`/`Execute` on the removed method silently succeed and return a callback channel that never fires instead of the "method %s not defined" error

**Standard:** "Do invariants still hold after every path?"

**Fix:** add `RemoveTriggerSubscriber`/`RemoveExecutableClient` methods to `CombinedClient` that delete the map entry, and have `pruneStaleShims` detach the stale method from `w.cachedShims.combinedClients[shimID{capID: key.capID, donID: key.donID}]` before closing it.

<!-- pr-coding-standards-review -->

**Medium** - Tests

the new tests exercise pruning only for trigger subscribers, trigger publishers, and combined clients; the executable-client and executable-server prune paths (`wanted.executableClients`/`wanted.executableServers` in `computeWantedShimKeys` and the corresponding `pruneStaleShims` loops) are never run, so a regression there (e.g. a wrong DON ID on the server-side key) would ship undetected

**Standard:** "Is new behaviour tested through its public interface, including error paths?"

**Fix:** add `OnNewRegistry`-driven tests that serve an executable capability (`RemoteExecutableConfig`) and remove its method/DON, asserting the server shim and dispatcher receiver are removed, plus a client-side `RemoteExecutableConfig` prune case.

<!-- pr-coding-standards-review -->
